scope: D021-D040; 12 Domain1 and 8 Domain2. Existing 360 A/B/C and W1 twenty compared.
notice: A verified web/PDF source location and author rationales are not equivalent to legal certification or comprehensive original USP chapter access.

items.source_citation: Board Policy 2026-03 §I numerical action tables (pp.1–2)
items.date_or_scope_watch: Policy 2026-03 strict > table in current policy; verify newer policy and USP before frozen.
items.legal_novelty_delta: ISO-classified viable/nonviable/surface action-level values at equality versus above threshold; multi-measurement classification.

all_four_option_checks.text: ISO Class 7 viable-air sample: 10 CFU per 1,000 L.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. The policy lists action as greater than 10 CFU for ISO 7 viable air. Ten equals, rather than exceeds, that threshold.

all_four_option_checks.text: ISO Class 5 surface sample: 4 CFU per media device.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. The policy defines ISO 5 surface action as greater than 3 CFU; four exceeds it.

all_four_option_checks.text: ISO Class 8 surface sample: 50 CFU per media device.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. The ISO 8 surface action threshold is greater than 50 CFU, not equal to 50.

all_four_option_checks.text: ISO Class 7 non-viable air: 352,001 particles of at least 0.5 micrometer per cubic meter.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. The ISO 7 nonviable action threshold is greater than 352,000 particles; the result exceeds it.

items.source_citation: Board Policy 2026-03 §III(G) (repeat action-level EM results within 60 days)
items.date_or_scope_watch: Confirm latest Board 60-day microbiologist requirement before exam date.
items.legal_novelty_delta: New requirement: repeat action-level in same ISO area within 60 days, including nonconsecutive excursions, triggers microbiologist.

all_four_option_checks.text: Engage a microbiologist after repeat action-level results in the same ISO area within 60 days.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. The policy mandates a microbiologist for repeat EM action-level results in the same ISO area within 60 days, consecutive or non-consecutive.

all_four_option_checks.text: Engage a microbiologist only when repeat samples occur at the exact same site on consecutive dates.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. The 60-day rule applies to the same ISO classified AREA, not only the identical surface and not only consecutive samples.

all_four_option_checks.text: Restart the monitoring clock because the two results were not consecutive.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. The express language covers both consecutive and non-consecutive repeats within the specified time.

all_four_option_checks.text: Postpone microbiologist review until at least three action-level samples have occurred.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. The policy triggers additional microbiologist engagement with a qualifying repeat; a third action result is not necessary.

items.source_citation: Board Policy 2026-03 §I; Board Environmental Monitoring Advisory §§I(A), II(A)
items.date_or_scope_watch: Board environmental monitoring Advisory dated revised Sept 3 2026; dynamic post-clean distinction.
items.legal_novelty_delta: Dynamic sampling plan during operating conditions versus misleading results taken immediately after a deep clean.

all_four_option_checks.text: Use risk-based sampling under representative dynamic operating conditions that reflect compounding activity.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. The Board advisory requires dynamic conditions, including ongoing work and personnel, and the policy calls for a risk-based plan.

all_four_option_checks.text: Accept the after-deep-clean data as sufficient evidence because fewer organisms will be recovered.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. Sampling immediately after a deep clean fails to capture meaningful dynamic production conditions.

all_four_option_checks.text: Work with a microbiologist or other qualified professional to choose the appropriate sites, times and sampling locations.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. The Board policy and advisory explicitly require a risk-based plan developed with qualified technical assistance.

all_four_option_checks.text: Eliminate surface samples if the air sampler returns zero organisms.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. The Board program encompasses viable air, surface, and nonviable air environmental monitoring as applicable.

items.source_citation: Board Policy 2026-03 §I (pass-through cleaner-space rule; ISO 7 nonviable table)
items.date_or_scope_watch: Cleaner-space pass-through and ISO7 numeric particles; action >352000; comply with nonviable suspension separately.
items.legal_novelty_delta: Cleaner adjacent ISO classification governs pass-through results; uses ISO7 vs ISO8 limits.

all_four_option_checks.text: Treat the result as below action because the pass-through door can be opened toward ISO 8.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. The pass-through is assessed according to the cleaner ISO classified space under the policy.

all_four_option_checks.text: Apply the ISO 8 limit if the staff are working in the ante-area at sampling.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. The sampling location's cleaner adjoining area, not the staff location, controls.

all_four_option_checks.text: Apply the cleaner ISO 7 threshold; 400,000 exceeds the 352,000 non-viable action level.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. Policy 2026-03 states pass-through action limits follow the cleaner-space ISO classification, so this is above the ISO 7 limit.

all_four_option_checks.text: Do not classify a pass-through sample under the policy's environmental monitoring tables.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. The policy includes pass-throughs and explicitly assigns their ISO action levels.

items.source_citation: Board Advisory: USP <800> in Community Pharmacies §§PPE, Handling, Spill Control, Waste; 247 CMR 9.01(3)
items.date_or_scope_watch: Board USP800 advisory 2022 applicable by 247 CMR 9.01(3); current USP original not directly authenticated.
items.legal_novelty_delta: Actual broken antineoplastic dosage-form powder exposure and response, distinct from intact handling and AOR.

all_four_option_checks.text: Apply the pharmacy's hazardous-drug spill/exposure control procedure and trained staff protections.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. Physical damage and powder exposure require the HD program's handling, PPE, cleaning and spill controls rather than ordinary intact tablet counting.

all_four_option_checks.text: Handle the fragments like any intact tablet because the patient-specific order is not a compounded prescription.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. The new exposure risk is not equivalent to handling the manufacturer-finished intact dosage form.

all_four_option_checks.text: Dispose of the powder in the regular sink to avoid further countertop handling.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. The Board advisory requires appropriate HD waste segregation and spill remediation; drain disposal is not a safe general method.

all_four_option_checks.text: Count the remaining broken tablets on a shared tray after wiping the surface with a dry cloth.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. Uncontrolled powder contamination is incompatible with required hazardous-handling SOPs and worker protection.

items.source_citation: Board Advisory: USP <800> in Community Pharmacies pp.1–3 (full containment cases, storage/handling)
items.date_or_scope_watch: Board 2022 advisory qualifies storage subject to pharmacy policies; don't confuse with contaminated packages.
items.legal_novelty_delta: Comparative storage permission for intact/reproductive HDs versus planned manipulations requiring full containment.

all_four_option_checks.text: Intact finished antineoplastic dosage forms may be stored with other medication under a suitable pharmacy policy.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. The Board advisory permits storage with other medicine for final antineoplastic dosage forms, subject to the pharmacy's policies and procedures.

all_four_option_checks.text: Antineoplastic HDs requiring future manipulation must be handled under full USP <800> containment strategies.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. The advisory explicitly lists storage of antineoplastic drugs needing future manipulation among full-containment situations.

all_four_option_checks.text: All reproductive-risk-only finished products require the same storage containment as hazardous bulk API used for compounding.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. The Board describes permitted co-storage of reproductive-risk-only products; it distinguishes API and manipulated antineoplastic conditions.

all_four_option_checks.text: A formal hazardous-drug program includes documented storage and handling procedures.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. The Board advisory calls for documented hazardous-drug storage, handling and related policies, including receipt, labeling and spill precautions.

items.source_citation: Board Advisory: USP <800> in Community Pharmacies §Training (p.3)
items.date_or_scope_watch: Board HD training and 12-month competency, not pharmacy CE; applicable role.
items.legal_novelty_delta: HD receiving staff's initial and at-least-annual documented function-specific competency, not hospital spill response.

all_four_option_checks.text: A mandatory pharmacist licensure examination taken every quarter.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. The Board's hazardous handling competency expectation is function-based, not a quarterly pharmacist license exam.

all_four_option_checks.text: A new manufacturer shipping agreement signed by the worker each time a delivery arrives.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. Manufacturer shipping contracts do not substitute for documented employee HD handling competencies.

all_four_option_checks.text: Documented reassessment of hazardous-drug competencies at least every 12 months.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. The Board advisory specifies initial assessment and reassessment at least every 12 months for staff independently handling HDs.

all_four_option_checks.text: Annual DEA Schedule II inventory certification for every receiving employee.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. The HD worker competency requirement is distinct from DEA inventory obligations.

items.source_citation: Board Advisory: USP <800> in Community Pharmacies pp.1–2 (C-PEC in negative pressure), 247 CMR 9.01(3)
items.date_or_scope_watch: Board advisory supports negative pressure for HD API compounding; confirm room and C-PEC in current operative USP if final release.
items.legal_novelty_delta: Negative-pressure engineering control ceases during active hazardous-API nonsterile compounding; AOR cannot replace failed containment.

all_four_option_checks.text: Continue compounding after documenting a fresh product-specific assessment of risk.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. The Board advisory states hazardous API compounding requires full containment; a reduced-containment risk assessment does not replace it.

all_four_option_checks.text: Continue if a second staff member verifies the weight of the hazardous ingredient.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. A checking step cannot restore missing environmental containment.

all_four_option_checks.text: Compound on an open weighing bench.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. The Board identifies containment equipment in a negative-pressure room for hazardous compounding.

all_four_option_checks.text: Restore and verify negative-pressure containment before compounding resumes.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. The pharmacy cannot substitute a reduced AOR for a missing negative-pressure containment system that is required for this manipulation.

items.source_citation: MA Board Memorandum 2025-11-06: Automated Non-Sterile Compounding Devices ¶1
items.date_or_scope_watch: Nov 6 2025 memo, device FDA approval applicability or manufacturer validation evidence.
items.legal_novelty_delta: Manufacturer validation evidence and FDA device-approval status under 2025 MA memo, distinct from 503A/503B inventory.

all_four_option_checks.text: Reject it because every device requires FDA clearance.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. The memorandum permits a documented manufacturer-validation pathway where FDA approval is not required or applicable.

all_four_option_checks.text: Check FDA approval requirements or documented manufacturer validation for the device.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. The Board memo asks the pharmacy to assess FDA approval status or other manufacturer validation documentation for nonsterile compounding.

all_four_option_checks.text: Use the device because a vendor advertises it as 'automated,' without checking validation.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. Marketing claims alone do not satisfy the pharmacy's documentation responsibility.

all_four_option_checks.text: Rely solely on a pharmacist's current license instead of reviewing device validation.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. Pharmacist credentials do not replace equipment validation and compounding-quality requirements.

items.source_citation: MA Board Memorandum 2025-11-06: Automated Non-Sterile Compounding Devices ¶¶1–2
items.date_or_scope_watch: Memo ingredient compatibility for approved API or approved IND product.
items.legal_novelty_delta: Device ingredient compatibility for FDA-approved API and IND ingredient, distinct from statutory ingredient eligibility.

all_four_option_checks.text: The pharmacy must confirm that each applicable FDA-approved API or approved-IND ingredient is compatible with the device.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. The memo imposes a separate ingredient compatibility check beyond equipment validation.

all_four_option_checks.text: Manufacturer device validation alone establishes compatibility for every possible substance.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. The Board's second item requires independent confirmation of component compatibility.

all_four_option_checks.text: Ingredient Y may be used without further review because its parent drug received FDA approval.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. FDA approval of an API does not itself demonstrate compatibility with the selected device.

all_four_option_checks.text: Ingredient Y should not be used until the pharmacy confirms device compatibility for that ingredient.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. A validated machine does not establish the safety or suitability of an unverified API on the ingredient-specific check.

items.source_citation: Board Memorandum 2025-11-06: Automated Non-Sterile Compounding Devices ¶3; 247 CMR 9.01(3)
items.date_or_scope_watch: Memo ¶3 readily-cleanable requirement; manufacturer validation does not waive residue-control.
items.legal_novelty_delta: Device cleaning and cross contamination for sequential batches, not documentation of ingredient lots.

all_four_option_checks.text: Continue production when the same trained technician operates both batches.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. The memo requires confirmation that the device is readily cleanable; a consistent operator does not replace residue controls.

all_four_option_checks.text: Use the manufacturer's marketing statement of accuracy to establish drug-residue clearance.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. Accuracy claims do not demonstrate cleanability or absence of cross-contamination.

all_four_option_checks.text: Resolve whether the machine is cleanable enough to minimize drug cross-contamination.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. The Board explicitly requires pharmacies to confirm device cleanability to minimize cross-contamination.

all_four_option_checks.text: Assign a shorter beyond-use date to the second product and skip the cleaning question.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. A changed BUD does not remedy possible cross-contamination introduced by uncleanable equipment.

items.source_citation: MA Board 2025-11-06 Automated Non-Sterile Compounding Devices memo; 247 CMR 9.01(3); MA Board Retail Pharmacy Inspection Template items 92–93; Board Policy 2023-07 §VI(B)
items.date_or_scope_watch: Board inspection template items 92-93 plus 2023-07 §VI; full USP795 subscription text not independently authenticated.
items.legal_novelty_delta: Automation does not transfer pharmacy quality and MFR/CR accountability to machine vendor.

all_four_option_checks.text: The pharmacy remains accountable for product quality and applicable compounding records.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. The Board memorandum expressly retains pharmacy responsibility regardless of equipment; 247 CMR 9.01(3) retains applicable USP compounding standards.

all_four_option_checks.text: The manufacturer assumes all final compounded-product accountability when it validates the machine.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. Validation does not transfer pharmacy responsibility to the maker.

all_four_option_checks.text: Device validation waives USP preparation records.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. The Board requires continued compliance with USP chapters despite automation.

all_four_option_checks.text: The pharmacy becomes an FDA-registered 503B outsourcing facility by purchasing the device.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. Federal 503B status is a separate registration model, not conferred by a device purchase.

items.source_citation: 21 CFR 1306.05(a) controlled-prescription required elements; 247 CMR 9.15(2); Board Policy 2018-01 §III(B)(vi)
items.date_or_scope_watch: 21 CFR 1306.05(a) NDC omitted not required; dosage form legally essential; no categorical new-Rx claim.
items.legal_novelty_delta: NDC is not a federally required controlled Rx field, but dosage form is; no prescriber/DEA amendment calculation.

all_four_option_checks.text: An NDC is not a required federal controlled-prescription element, so its absence alone does not invalidate Rx A.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. 21 CFR 1306.05(a) lists patient/prescriber identifiers and drug name, strength, dosage form, quantity and directions, but not an NDC.

all_four_option_checks.text: Rx B includes its NDC, so the dosage-form omission can be ignored without further evaluation.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. A product NDC does not substitute for the dosage form listed in 21 CFR 1306.05(a).

all_four_option_checks.text: Rx B lacks a required federal prescription element until the dosage form is properly established.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. The dosage form is expressly listed as required information, despite the optional NDC being present.

all_four_option_checks.text: Both prescriptions are invalid because DEA requires a separate NDC printed on every controlled Rx.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. NDC is not one of the enumerated mandatory prescription fields under the federal controlled-prescription rule.

items.date_or_scope_watch: 21 CFR 1311.170(e) transmitted data integrity distinct from allowed lossless format conversion.
items.legal_novelty_delta: A data field dropped by transmission intermediary invalidates EPCS even though lossless format conversion is permitted; not post-sign application alteration.

all_four_option_checks.text: The prescription remains valid because all electronic field conversions are exempt from audit.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. Changing data structure is permissible; losing required Part 1306 content is not.

all_four_option_checks.text: Reconstruct the quantity from the patient's last fill and proceed without prescriber authorization.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. A prior record does not repair an invalid prescription whose required data were altered in transmission.

all_four_option_checks.text: A patient's recollection supplies the missing quantity.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. Patient recollection is not prescriber authentication for missing required controlled prescription content.

all_four_option_checks.text: Loss of a required prescription field invalidates the transmitted EPCS order.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. 21 CFR 1311.170(e) treats changed, truncated or removed required content during electronic transmission as invalid, while permitting lossless format conversions.

items.date_or_scope_watch: 21 CFR 1306.04 corresponding responsibility; no automatic dispense/refusal based on one signal.
items.legal_novelty_delta: Authentic DEA identity and e-signature do not resolve material legitimate-medical-purpose red flags; requires pharmacist inquiry.

all_four_option_checks.text: Dispense because the prescriber signature and DEA registration are valid.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. 21 CFR 1306.04(a) requires legitimate medical purpose and places a corresponding duty on the pharmacist; a valid number does not resolve an unexplained substantive red flag.

all_four_option_checks.text: Hold dispensing and investigate unresolved medical-purpose concerns using appropriate evidence.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. Authenticity and registration are not substitutes for a good-faith legitimacy inquiry when material red flags remain.

all_four_option_checks.text: Ask the technician to determine whether the patient's diagnosis justifies all controlled prescriptions.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. Technician data collection does not replace the pharmacist's professional legal and clinical responsibility.

all_four_option_checks.text: Call the insurer for payment confirmation and regard approval as a medical-purpose finding.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. Financial adjudication does not establish legitimate medical purpose under the DEA rule.

items.source_citation: MA Board/DCP Policy 2018-01 §§II(C)–(D), III(A)(i)(c), IV
items.date_or_scope_watch: Board/DCP 2018-01 revised 2024: patient address changed with authorized agent vs prescriber name/signature never amended.
items.legal_novelty_delta: Authorized agent may confirm patient address change but cannot replace originating prescriber identity/signature.

all_four_option_checks.text: Rewrite the prescriber's identity and signature because both physicians share the clinic.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. The policy bars changing a prescriber's name or signature on prescriptions in any Schedule II–VI.

all_four_option_checks.text: Correct the patient's street address after consultation with the prescriber or authorized agent, with required documentation.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. Board/DCP Policy 2018-01 permits a changed patient address with consultation, including an authorized agent.

all_four_option_checks.text: Request a new prescription if the intent is to substitute the other prescriber as the issuing practitioner.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. The originating prescriber identity/signature is non-correctable and requires a new prescription to change.

all_four_option_checks.text: Treat the office employee's statement as a substitute for a new prescription signed by the different physician.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. An employee callback cannot replace issuing a lawful new prescription when a prohibited field is changed.

items.date_or_scope_watch: 2026 Aug 12 temporary O-DSMT placement ends Aug 2028 unless changed; verify on actual exam date.
items.legal_novelty_delta: Temporary 2026 DEA Schedule I O-DSMT versus parent tramadol IV; parent metabolite scheduling differs.

all_four_option_checks.text: Tramadol Schedule III; O-desmethyltramadol Schedule III.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. Tramadol is Schedule IV; the metabolite has a separate temporary Schedule I listing.

all_four_option_checks.text: Both are Schedule IV because DEA schedules active metabolites with parent medicines.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. A distinct scheduling action placed O-DSMT in Schedule I effective August 12, 2026.

all_four_option_checks.text: Tramadol Schedule IV; O-desmethyltramadol temporarily Schedule I.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. Tramadol is controlled under 21 CFR 1308.14(b)(3); O-DSMT was temporarily placed in Schedule I in 2026.

all_four_option_checks.text: Neither is scheduled because the metabolite occurs during legitimate therapy.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. Metabolism does not exempt a separately listed manufactured/handled substance from the CSA.

items.source_citation: FDA AUVELITY label (2026) §9.1; 105 CMR 700.002(F); 105 CMR 700.012; DPH PMP pharmacy reporting
items.date_or_scope_watch: 2026 AUVELITY label FDA section 9.1 and current MA MassPAT requirements; reportability differs from gabapentin.
items.legal_novelty_delta: FDA-labeled dextromethorphan/bupropion product is federal unscheduled MA VI, unlike MassPAT-reportable gabapentin.

all_four_option_checks.text: Schedule V, with regular Massachusetts PMP submission.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. Dextromethorphan/bupropion is not federally controlled as specified in the FDA label.

all_four_option_checks.text: Schedule VI; not subject to routine MassPAT reporting absent an added reportable ingredient.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. Massachusetts Schedule VI covers prescription drugs outside I–V; DPH requires reporting for II–V and gabapentin, not each VI prescription.

all_four_option_checks.text: Federal noncontrolled and Massachusetts Schedule VI; every VI drug must be reported to MassPAT.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. MA reporting requirements do not extend to all Schedule VI drugs; gabapentin is the specifically identified drug of concern.

all_four_option_checks.text: Federal Schedule II and Massachusetts Schedule II because it is indicated for neuropsychiatric treatment.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. Clinical indication does not determine CSA Schedule; the FDA label states no controlled substances.

items.source_citation: 21 CFR 1308.14(c)(10); 21 CFR 1308.31–.32; DEA Exempted Prescription Product Table (chlordiazepoxide/clidinium); FDA Librax Drug Abuse and Dependence label; 105 CMR 700.002(F)
items.date_or_scope_watch: Actual on DEA exempt list and FDA Librax label; product NDC exemption must be verified at use, and federal and MA classifications differentiated.
items.legal_novelty_delta: Chlordiazepoxide/clidinium's DEA exempted prescription-product status versus pure chlordiazepoxide, rather than Fioricet NDC exemption.

all_four_option_checks.text: Both products must be Schedule IV because they contain chlordiazepoxide.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. A specifically exempted finished combination is treated differently from the separately controlled benzodiazepine ingredient.

all_four_option_checks.text: Neither product can be scheduled because antispasmodic drugs are outside CSA regulations.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. Chlordiazepoxide itself remains federal Schedule IV.

all_four_option_checks.text: LIBRAX becomes Schedule II because it contains an anticholinergic ingredient.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. Combining drugs does not make the product Schedule II absent an applicable classification.

all_four_option_checks.text: Chlordiazepoxide alone is IV; listed LIBRAX is federally exempt and MA Schedule VI.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. DEA's active product-specific exemption removes qualifying Librax from federal Schedule IV; MA Schedule VI applies to prescription drugs not scheduled I–V.

items.source_citation: FDA VIVITROL controlled substance status; FDA BRIXADI 2026 label §§5.2–5.3; 21 CFR 1308.13(e)(2); MA 105 CMR 700.002
items.date_or_scope_watch: Brixadi 2026 label and active REMS, Vivitrol FDA naltrexone labeling; active REMS may change.
items.legal_novelty_delta: New long-acting OUD injections naltrexone not controlled (MA VI) and buprenorphine III with Brixadi REMS direct-to-provider.

all_four_option_checks.text: VIVITROL is not federally controlled and falls under Massachusetts Schedule VI as an ordinary prescription drug.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. FDA's Vivitrol label states it is not a controlled substance; Massachusetts places other prescription drugs into Schedule VI.

all_four_option_checks.text: BRIXADI is a federal Schedule III buprenorphine product and its REMS restricts dispensing directly to a healthcare provider for administration.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Correct. The FDA Brixadi label identifies the Schedule III substance and direct-to-provider REMS distribution controls.

all_four_option_checks.text: Both are federal Schedule II simply because they are used to treat opioid-use disorder.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. An indication for OUD does not set the drug's schedule; naltrexone is not controlled and buprenorphine is III.

all_four_option_checks.text: The pharmacist may dispense BRIXADI directly to the patient for unsupervised self-injection when the prescription is valid.
all_four_option_checks.author_rationale: Incorrect. The FDA BRIXADI REMS forbids direct patient dispensing and requires provider administration.
